chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah who said:

(He) mentioned that Bureyra was a slave of Ayesha and had a husband for her who was a slave. So when she was emancipated, Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to her: ‘Choose! If you so desire to you can stay with your husband, and if your so desire to, so no’.

key_terms.بَرِيرَةَ: Bureyra, a specific historical figure and slave of Ayesha

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a slave woman's marriage when she is emancipated but her husband remains a slave?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the legal principle of 'ikhtiyar' (choice), granting an emancipated slave woman the autonomy to decide whether to maintain her marital bond with her still-enslaved husband or to separate. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling highlights that the disparity in status breaks the automatic continuity of the marriage, allowing the woman to choose based on her preference, a principle derived directly from the Prophet's instruction to Barirah. This case is frequently cited by scholars to illustrate the intersection of manumission, marital rights, and the specific conditions under which a slave marriage is dissolved or preserved.
